# How many contestants are shown up close?

## Short answer

**Two.** Exactly two contestants of the game show are shown in close-up in this
video: a dark-haired young woman captioned **"VALENTINA"**, and a **blonde
woman whom the host addresses as "Laura."** A third person is also shown in
close-up — the man in the grey jacket and glasses — but he is the show's **host**
(Carlo Conti), not a contestant, so he is not included in the count.

(See the caveat at the end: on a strict reading of who is actually *playing* the
game, the blonde "Laura" is the show's on-stage assistant rather than a
contestant, which would make the answer **one**. Two is the count of
non-host people shown up close.)

## What the video is

The clip is from the Italian RAI 1 quiz show **L'Eredità** — the title logo
"L'EREDITÀ" is shown in the opening seconds (roughly 0.9 s–4.3 s). The segment is
the show's true/false round: an orange banner across the bottom reads
*"A PITTSBURGH HA APERTO IL 'CONFLICT KITCHEN': UN RISTORANTE DOVE LE COPPIE
POSSONO LITIGARE LIBERAMENTE"*, with **VERO** (left) and **FALSO** (right)
buttons. English subtitles translate the dialogue.

## Shot-by-shot breakdown (the whole 54.5 s accounted for)

I detected every scene cut in the video and checked each shot. There are only
nine shots, and only **three** of them are close-ups of a person:

| Time | Shot | Person shown up close |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0 – 0.9 s | Black | — |
| 0.9 – 4.3 s | "L'EREDITÀ" title graphic | — |
| 4.3 – 5.2 s | Close-up of a blue set fixture (a lit pole), no face | — |
| **5.2 – 12.5 s** | **Close-up** | **Contestant "Valentina"** (brunette, white flower in her hair, dark off-shoulder top; her name caption "VALENTINA" is on screen at ~5–6 s). She hears the statement and answers *"False, false."* |
| **12.5 – 15.3 s** | **Close-up** | **The host, Carlo Conti** (grey jacket, dark shirt, glasses) reading out the statement — *not* a contestant |
| **15.3 – 19.4 s** | **Close-up** | **Valentina again** (same person, not a new one) |
| 19.4 – 22.8 s | Wide overhead shot of the circular studio | — |
| **22.8 – 49.8 s** | **Close-up** | **The blonde "Laura"** (grey sleeveless top, black-and-white striped scarf), who explains what Conflict Kitchen is |
| 49.8 – 54.5 s | Wide overhead shot of the studio, then black | — |

So the total number of **distinct people** shown up close is **three**, of which
**one is the host**, leaving **two** who are not the host.

## Why the man is not counted

The man in the close-up at 12.5–15.3 s is the presenter, Carlo Conti. Two things
confirm it: he is the one *reading the question* ("…a restaurant where couples
can fight openly"), and in the overhead wide shots he is the single figure
standing on the raised circular platform in the **centre** of the arena, wearing
the same light grey jacket, while the players stand at podiums around the rim.

## How many contestants are in the studio overall

For contrast, the wide overhead shots (19.4–22.8 s and 49.8–52 s) show **six
contestants** standing at red podiums around the circular stage, plus the host in
the middle. Only one or two of those six are ever brought to the camera in
close-up, which is why the "up close" count is much smaller than the number of
people playing.

## Caveat on "Laura"

There is a genuine ambiguity about the blonde woman. Evidence that she is *not* a
contestant but the show's on-stage assistant (on *L'Eredità* these assistants are
called **"professoresse"**, and their documented job is precisely to give the
explanation of each answer alongside the host — the blonde "Laura" of that era
was Laura Forgia, a professoressa from 2011 to 2016):

- She does not answer the question; she delivers a long, encyclopaedic
  explanation of what Conflict Kitchen is, with her eyes repeatedly dropping as
  if reading from a card.
- The host prompts her by name and then says *"Very good… thank you, Laura,"*
  which is how a presenter hands off to and back from an assistant.
- She never gets an on-screen name caption, while the contestant Valentina does.
- In the wide shots, none of the six people at the podiums matches her (grey top,
  bare arms, very long blonde hair); the blonde at the right-hand podium is
  wearing a bright yellow top. A blonde woman in a pale outfit is instead seated
  **outside** the contestants' ring at the far left of frame.

If you count only people actually competing, the answer is therefore **one**
contestant shown up close (Valentina). If you count, as a viewer naturally would,
every close-up of someone on the show other than the host, the answer is **two**.

**Stated plainly: two contestants are shown up close; three people in total are
shown up close, the third being the host.**
